title: Esports Ecosystem Atlas
description: A curriculum-focused map of publishers, tournament operators, competitions, education pathways, teams, careers, broadcast and commercial relationships.

curriculumPresets.title: Full esports ecosystem
curriculumPresets.description: Explore how rights holders, competitions, operators, teams, talent, education, media and commercial partners interact.

curriculumPresets.title: L2 Unit 1: games, teams and tournaments
curriculumPresets.description: Identify tournament structures, current titles, team roles and organising bodies, then compare two competition pathways.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 1: introduction to esports
curriculumPresets.description: Investigate the size, structure, technology, roles and related industries that make esports an ecosystem rather than only competitive play.

curriculumPresets.title: L3 Unit 5: esports events
curriculumPresets.description: Follow the dependencies between rights holder, operator, venue, officials, production, platform, teams and audience. Use the map to build an event responsibility matrix.

curriculumPresets.title: Enterprise, careers and branding
curriculumPresets.description: Connect L2 Unit 5 and L3 Units 3, 7, 10 and 11 through revenue, sponsorship, audience, brand, social media, casting and employability roles.

nodes.name: Esports Ecosystem
nodes.note: Esports depends on game ownership, organised competition, teams, technology, media, audiences and commercial support.
nodes.hook: Select one event and identify who owns the game, runs the event, competes, broadcasts and pays.

nodes.name: Publishers and Rights Holders
nodes.note: Publishers control game intellectual property and usually set or license official competition rules.
nodes.hook: Explain how publisher ownership makes esports governance different from many traditional sports.

nodes.name: Riot Games
nodes.note: Riot operates official ecosystems for League of Legends and VALORANT.
nodes.hook: Compare one publisher-operated circuit with a third-party operated circuit.

nodes.name: League of Legends Esports
nodes.note: League of Legends has regional and international organised competition.
nodes.hook: Trace qualification from a regional league to an international event.

nodes.name: VALORANT Champions Tour
nodes.note: VCT is Riot’s official global VALORANT competition pathway.
nodes.hook: Identify open, regional and international stages in the current pathway.

nodes.name: VALORANT Game Changers
nodes.note: Game Changers is a complementary competition pathway within VALORANT esports.
nodes.hook: Assess how targeted pathways can broaden participation.

nodes.name: Valve
nodes.note: Valve owns Counter-Strike and licenses a tournament ecosystem with external operators.
nodes.hook: Compare publisher control with operator responsibility.

nodes.name: Counter-Strike
nodes.note: Counter-Strike’s competitive ecosystem includes Valve Majors and operator circuits.
nodes.hook: Differentiate a game title, circuit, tournament and match.

nodes.name: Epic Games / Psyonix
nodes.note: Psyonix runs Rocket League esports under Epic Games ownership.
nodes.hook: Investigate how game updates can affect competitive integrity.

nodes.name: Rocket League Championship Series
nodes.note: RLCS is the official Rocket League competition circuit.
nodes.hook: Map an RLCS season from online qualification to Major or World Championship.

nodes.name: Blizzard Entertainment
nodes.note: Blizzard owns Overwatch and publishes the official OWCS structure.
nodes.hook: Identify what the publisher delegates to regional operators.

nodes.name: Overwatch Champions Series
nodes.note: OWCS is the current official Overwatch competition circuit.
nodes.hook: Compare its regional stages and international qualification.

nodes.name: EA SPORTS
nodes.note: EA publishes the FC Pro competition rules for EA SPORTS FC.
nodes.hook: Use rules to identify eligibility, platform and conduct requirements.

nodes.name: FC Pro
nodes.note: FC Pro is the official EA SPORTS FC competitive programme.
nodes.hook: Compare individual and team-based competition requirements.

nodes.name: Tournament Operators
nodes.note: Operators deliver brackets, rules administration, officials, venues, production and participant services.
nodes.hook: Build a RACI matrix for a tournament operator and rights holder.

nodes.name: ESL FACEIT Group
nodes.note: EFG combines major tournament-operation and competitive-platform brands.
nodes.hook: Identify platform, event, production and commercial functions within the group.

nodes.name: Intel Extreme Masters
nodes.note: IEM is a long-running international tournament brand.
nodes.hook: Use IEM Cologne 2026 to identify organiser, game owner, title sponsor and venue.

nodes.name: Education and Grassroots
nodes.note: School, college and university competitions create participation and development pathways.
nodes.hook: Compare the aims and eligibility of school/college and university competitions.

nodes.name: British Esports
nodes.note: British Esports supports UK pathways, education and the Student Champs.
nodes.hook: Identify governing, education, event and community functions.

nodes.name: Student Champs 2026/27
nodes.note: The 2026/27 Champs lists League of Legends, Overwatch 2, Rocket League, Marvel Rivals and age-restricted VALORANT team competitions.
nodes.hook: Compare team size, age rules and match format for two current titles.

nodes.name: National Student Esports
nodes.note: NSE provides a UK higher-education competition and community pathway.
nodes.hook: Check current eligibility and explain why verification matters.

nodes.name: Competition Delivery
nodes.note: A competition converts game rules into formats, schedules, seeding, officiating and results.
nodes.hook: Design a format and justify fairness, time, venue and broadcast trade-offs.

nodes.name: Formats and Brackets
nodes.note: Round robin, Swiss, groups and elimination formats create different competitive and scheduling properties.
nodes.hook: Simulate eight teams under two formats and compare match count and elimination risk.

nodes.name: Rules and Competitive Integrity
nodes.note: Eligibility, anti-cheat, pauses, disputes and sanctions support credible results.
nodes.hook: Write an evidence chain for resolving one match dispute.

nodes.name: Event Operations
nodes.note: Event delivery coordinates venue, stage, networking, hardware, safety, staffing and schedules.
nodes.hook: Identify three single points of failure and propose contingencies.

nodes.name: Teams, Talent and Careers
nodes.note: Competitive and production outcomes depend on specialist playing, coaching, operational, creative and technical roles.
nodes.hook: Map one role’s responsibilities, evidence of skill and progression route.

nodes.name: Players and Teams
nodes.note: Players compete within rosters, contracts, practice structures and team culture.
nodes.hook: Compare in-game role, team role and employment responsibility.

nodes.name: Coaching and Performance
nodes.note: Coaches and analysts turn game data, review and practice into strategy and development.
nodes.hook: Create a review cycle from replay evidence to a measurable training goal.

nodes.name: Admins and Officials
nodes.note: Tournament admins enforce rules, manage lobbies and resolve incidents.
nodes.hook: Write a decision log that separates observation, rule and ruling.

nodes.name: Shoutcasters and Analysts
nodes.note: On-air talent explains action, builds narrative and serves different audience knowledge levels.
nodes.hook: Produce a play-by-play line and an analytical follow-up for the same clip.

nodes.name: Media and Audience
nodes.note: Broadcast and social platforms connect live competition to audiences, communities and measurable engagement.
nodes.hook: Trace one match from game server through production to audience interaction.

nodes.name: Live Broadcast Production
nodes.note: Observers, directors, audio, graphics, replay and streaming systems turn matches into programmes.
nodes.hook: Allocate essential roles for a small student broadcast and justify each one.

nodes.name: Twitch distribution
nodes.note: Twitch is a major live distribution and audience-interaction platform for esports.
nodes.hook: Evaluate discoverability, moderation and analytics for an event channel.

nodes.name: YouTube Live distribution
nodes.note: YouTube supports live and on-demand distribution around the same event content.
nodes.hook: Compare live reach with the value of searchable archives and highlights.

nodes.name: Commercial and Support
nodes.note: Revenue and support can include sponsorship, media rights, ticketing, merchandise, publisher funding and services.
nodes.hook: Build a value exchange showing what each partner gives and receives.

nodes.name: Sponsors and Partners
nodes.note: Partners exchange funding, products or services for rights, activation and audience association.
nodes.hook: Design a sponsorship inventory without promising unverifiable audience outcomes.

nodes.name: Brand and Social Media
nodes.note: Brand identity and social content connect teams, events, communities and partners.
nodes.hook: Create a platform-specific content plan tied to one measurable objective.

nodes.name: Esports Enterprise
nodes.note: Esports ventures need a value proposition, target market, resources, finance, legal awareness and risk controls.
nodes.hook: Test a venture idea using customer evidence and a basic cost model.
